input_oneliner: 34M admitted for leg cellulitis, day 2, new periumbilical pain since evening now settling in RLQ, anorexic, T 38.1

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask: did the pain start periumbilical and migrate to the right lower quadrant; anorexia and nausea
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Migration of pain is among the most useful historical features for appendicitis

reference_targets_freetext.item: RLQ tenderness with rebound and percussion tenderness; cough test
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: RLQ tenderness and peritoneal signs carry the highest likelihood ratios for appendicitis
Retrocecal or pelvic appendix irritation; modest LR+ but cheap to elicit
Referred RLQ pain with LLQ palpation supports localized peritoneal irritation

reference_targets_freetext.item: Costovertebral angle tenderness and ask about dysuria or hematuria
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Separates pyelonephritis or stone from an intra-abdominal source

reference_targets_freetext.item: Abdominal rigidity and generalized peritonitis check
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Rigidity raises concern for perforation and changes urgency

off_bedside_acceptable: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
should_not_recommend: CT abdomen before abdominal exam and vitals
Withholding analgesia to preserve the abdominal exam
Enema or laxative for presumed constipation
